command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp MPLCONFIGDIR=/tmp/mpl
cd /tmp

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).
# No PATH export: aarchsci env images already have their python first.

echo "== staged bytes must match their pins =="
sha256sum -c pins.sha256 || { echo "FAIL: a staged file does not match its pin"; exit 1; }

python3 -u - <<'PYEOF' 2>&1 | tee grib.log
import sys, numpy as np, xarray as xr

def ver(p):
    try:
        from importlib.metadata import version
        return version(p)
    except Exception:
        return "unknown"
for p in ("cfgrib", "eccodes", "metpy", "xarray", "pint"):
    print("version\t%s %s" % (p, ver(p)))

GRIB = "gfs.pgrb2.1p00.f000"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- decode vs the publisher's manifest
# NOAA ships a wgrib2 inventory beside the file: one line per message. Checking what eccodes
# decodes against that is decode statistics against an EXTERNAL statement of the contents,
# rather than against the same library that did the decoding.
inv = [l for l in open(GRIB + ".idx") if l.strip()]
want = {}
for l in inv:
    f = l.split(":")
    if len(f) > 4:
        want[f[3]] = want.get(f[3], 0) + 1
print("inventory_messages\t%d" % len(inv))
for v in ("HGT", "TMP", "RH"):
    print("inventory_%s\t%d" % (v, want.get(v, 0)))

# TWO cfgrib SETTINGS, BOTH LOAD-BEARING.
#
# indexpath="": cfgrib otherwise writes an index cache NEXT TO the input, and a staged input is
# owned by the instance user while the container runs as the image's user -- the write fails
# with EPERM on a file the task never created.
#
# ONE shortName PER OPEN: a GFS file carries variables on DIFFERENT vertical coordinates (here
# 33 isobaric levels for most, 22 for some), and asking cfgrib for all isobaric variables at
# once makes it raise DatasetBuildError internally, silently DROP the incompatible ones, and
# carry on. That is not merely noisy -- the surviving merged `isobaricInhPa` coordinate would
# then be used to index arrays that may not share it, so a level mask could select different
# pressures for T than for RH and produce a wrong thickness with no error at all. Opening each
# field separately and asserting the three level vectors are IDENTICAL removes the ambiguity.
def load(short):
    return xr.open_dataset(
        GRIB, engine="cfgrib",
        backend_kwargs={"indexpath": "",
                        "filter_by_keys": {"typeOfLevel": "isobaricInhPa", "shortName": short}})

dsT, dsR, dsH = load("t"), load("r"), load("gh")
VT, VR, VH = "t", "r", "gh"
for nm, dd, vv in (("T", dsT, VT), ("RH", dsR, VR), ("HGT", dsH, VH)):
    if vv not in dd.data_vars:
        sys.exit("FAIL: %s not decoded from shortName=%s" % (nm, vv))
    print("decoded\t%-4s %s on %d isobaric levels" % (nm, vv, dd.isobaricInhPa.size))

levT = dsT.isobaricInhPa.values
levR = dsR.isobaricInhPa.values
levH = dsH.isobaricInhPa.values
if not (np.array_equal(levT, levR) and np.array_equal(levT, levH)):
    sys.exit("FAIL: T, RH and HGT are on different pressure levels (%d/%d/%d) -- any level mask "
             "would compare different altitudes" % (levT.size, levR.size, levH.size))
print("identity_levels\tT, RH and HGT share an identical pressure-level vector (%d levels)" % levT.size)

ds = dsT   # for the shared coordinate below
lev = levT
nlev_in_range = int(((lev >= 500) & (lev <= 1000)).sum())
print("levels_1000_to_500\t%d" % nlev_in_range)
if nlev_in_range < 8:
    sys.exit("FAIL: only %d levels between 1000 and 500 hPa; the integral would be too coarse"
             % nlev_in_range)

# Every HGT/TMP/RH message in the inventory should be decodable. cfgrib's isobaric subset will
# not contain surface or other level types, so compare the isobaric count rather than the total.
iso_count = {"TMP": int(dsT.isobaricInhPa.size), "RH": int(dsR.isobaricInhPa.size), "HGT": int(dsH.isobaricInhPa.size)}
for v, n in iso_count.items():
    print("decoded_isobaric_%s\t%d" % (v, n))
    if n == 0:
        sys.exit("FAIL: no isobaric %s levels decoded" % v)

# ---------------------------------------------------------- the file checked against itself
# The hypsometric equation ties geopotential thickness to the temperature and humidity field:
#     Z(500) - Z(1000) = (Rd/g) * integral of Tv dln(p)
# GFS carries BOTH sides -- its own geopotential heights and its own T/RH -- so the file can be
# checked for internal consistency. This is an independent field verifying the computation
# rather than a band on an observed value.
import metpy.calc as mpcalc
from metpy.units import units

sel = [(40.0, 260.0), (0.0, 180.0), (-45.0, 30.0), (60.0, 350.0), (20.0, 100.0)]
mask = (lev >= 500) & (lev <= 1000)
order = np.argsort(-lev[mask])          # descending pressure: 1000 -> 500
plev = lev[mask][order]

worst = 0.0
rows = []
for la, lo in sel:
    T  = dsT[VT].sel(latitude=la, longitude=lo, method="nearest").values[mask][order]
    RH = dsR[VR].sel(latitude=la, longitude=lo, method="nearest").values[mask][order]
    Z  = dsH[VH].sel(latitude=la, longitude=lo, method="nearest")
    z1000 = float(Z.sel(isobaricInhPa=1000.0, method="nearest").values)
    z500  = float(Z.sel(isobaricInhPa=500.0,  method="nearest").values)
    model = z500 - z1000

    p_q  = plev * units.hPa
    T_q  = (T * units.kelvin)
    rh_q = np.clip(RH, 0.0, 100.0) * units.percent
    w    = mpcalc.mixing_ratio_from_relative_humidity(p_q, T_q, rh_q)
    calc = float(mpcalc.thickness_hydrostatic(p_q, T_q, mixing_ratio=w).to("m").magnitude)

    rel = abs(calc - model) / abs(model)
    worst = max(worst, rel)
    rows.append((la, lo, model, calc, rel))
    print("point\tlat %6.1f lon %6.1f  model %8.2f m  hypsometric %8.2f m  rel %.4f"
          % (la, lo, model, calc, rel))

print("thickness_max_rel_dev\t%.5f" % worst)
# The band is set by the DISCRETISATION, not by what the numbers happened to do: the model
# integrates its own hydrostatic equation on ~127 native levels, this reproduces it from the
# 13 archived isobaric levels with a trapezoidal rule. A few tenths of a percent is the
# expected cost of that; 2% is comfortably above it and far below any real inconsistency.
if worst > 0.02:
    sys.exit("FAIL: hypsometric thickness and the file's own geopotential disagree by %.4f" % worst)
print("consistency\tGFS geopotential agrees with its own T/RH field through the hypsometric equation")

# ------------------------------------------------- an exact involution, needing no second field
# Potential temperature is invertible: theta(p,T) then T(p,theta) must return T. Holds whatever
# the data are, so it survives any change of fixture.
Tin = dsT[VT].sel(latitude=40.0, longitude=260.0, method="nearest").values[mask][order] * units.kelvin
th  = mpcalc.potential_temperature(plev * units.hPa, Tin)
Tb  = mpcalc.temperature_from_potential_temperature(plev * units.hPa, th)
inv_dev = float(np.nanmax(np.abs(Tb.to("kelvin").magnitude - Tin.magnitude)))
print("involution_theta_max_abs_K\t%.3e" % inv_dev)
if inv_dev > 1e-9:
    sys.exit("FAIL: potential-temperature round trip is not an involution (%.3e K)" % inv_dev)
print("identity_theta\ttheta(p,T) -> T(p,theta) returns T exactly")

with open("score.tsv", "w") as fh:
    fh.write("observable\tvalue\n")
    fh.write("inventory_messages\t%d\n" % len(inv))
    fh.write("pressure_levels\t%d\n" % levT.size)
    fh.write("levels_1000_to_500\t%d\n" % nlev_in_range)
    for la, lo, m, c, r in rows:
        fh.write("thickness_%s_%s\tmodel %.2f m, hypsometric %.2f m, rel %.5f\n" % (la, lo, m, c, r))
    fh.write("thickness_max_rel_dev\t%.5f\n" % worst)
    fh.write("involution_theta_max_abs_K\t%.3e\n" % inv_dev)

print("GRIB2 OK")
PYEOF
test "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" = "0" || { echo "FAIL: the GRIB2 check failed"; exit 1; }
cp score.tsv gfs-diag.txt
uname -m | awk '{print "arch\t"$1}'
echo "DONE"
